topics.title: [grug] Add hero launch controls for a context-length switch
topics.body:
The scaling-ladder launcher takes --seq-len and holds 4,194,304 tokens per rack per update, so the sequence batch shrinks as the context grows (2816 sequences at 16K on 11 racks). The step count (390251), learning rates, decay, and gate/router weight decay therefore match the 4K run. A changed context requires an explicit --qk-mult, applied to all attention layers; --capacity-factor overrides the expert receiver capacity. A resume at a new context also requires --context-switch-step and --flops-baseline-step/--flops-baseline-total. The new prior_context_phases argument of harrier_mix_2026_08_18_data_config turns the switch step into LmDataConfig.prior_context_phases, with the Harrier stage schedule at the 4K batch size and the 4K shuffle blocks, so the Harrier sources continue from their 4K reads. Hero eval stays at 4K packing. A context switch is rejected for runs below the 1e23-FLOP simulated-epoching cutoff, because the data offsets assume each source reads its whole cache.

trigger_hero.sh records the context, batch, QK multiplier, capacity, eval context, FLOPs baseline, and context switch step in the W&B lineage and the #8506 launch record.

The live run is unchanged: trigger_hero.sh still launches at 4K. A switch still needs a GPU rehearsal from the handoff checkpoint and agreed trial thresholds; see the inventory and validation plan in #9615.

Stacked on #9890, which is stacked on #9888. Part of #9615

comments.body:
🤖 `CONTEXT_SWITCH_STEP` can record only one context switch, and the plan in #8435 has two (4K → 8K at ~50%, then → 65K at ~95%). The launcher turns the step into a single `HarrierPriorContext(end_step=step, seq_len=4096, ...)` ([launch_scaling_ladder.py](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44782f64d32a043b2f3ad7f2aa8d64e8bf08cefa/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/launch_scaling_ladder.py#L231-L240)), so the second switch has no checked-in place for the intermediate phase.

The current check does not catch this. Suppose the run switches 4K → 16K at N1 and 16K → 64K at N2, and the second deploy PR sets `SEQ_LEN=65536` and keeps `CONTEXT_SWITCH_STEP=N1`. The check in [trigger_hero.sh](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44782f64d32a043b2f3ad7f2aa8d64e8bf08cefa/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/trigger_hero.sh#L107-L111) passes, because N1 is nonzero and before the handoff. The offsets are then computed as if the run went 4K → 64K at N1. Each source resumes inside the shuffle window it was reading at N2 instead of skipping to the next window, so it re-reads part of that window under a new within-window order. Stage boundaries at the 64K batch size are also not reconciled with the 16K phase. This is from reading the code; I have not run it.

`LmDataConfig.prior_phases` from #9888 already takes several phases and carries offsets forward across them (`test_second_context_switch_continues_past_the_first_switch_skip`). Only the trigger and launcher need to change. Suggestion:

- Replace `CONTEXT_SWITCH_STEP` with a checked-in history, for example `CONTEXT_HISTORY="4096:N1 16384:N2"` (each entry is the length the run trained at and the step at which it ended), and build one `HarrierPriorContext` per entry. A context-switch deploy PR then appends an entry, in the same way a handoff PR edits `HANDOFF_CHECKPOINT`, so the run's behavior stays determined by the launch commit.
- In the trigger, reject a history whose end steps do not increase, whose last end step is after the handoff checkpoint, or whose adjacent entries (and the last entry and `SEQ_LEN`) have the same length.
- Add a test that pins the reconstructed `PriorDataPhase` (stage steps, weights, shuffle) for a fixed history. The old phases are re-derived from `_stage_weights` and `_shuffle_config` at each launch, so a later edit to those functions would change the offsets of a run that already switched.

topics.title: [levanter] Continue mixture reads across a context-length switch
topics.body:
Harrier's shuffle blocks change from a fixed 256 sequences to a fixed 2^20 tokens (io_block_size = 2**20 // seq_len). At 4K the two are identical, so the live run's data order is unchanged. At a longer context, the token-sized blocks keep the outer block permutation the same, and only the order of sequences inside each 512-block shuffle window changes. With the old 256-sequence blocks, a 16K relaunch would have re-read an estimated 2.85T already-seen tokens of the remaining ~9T.

The new LmDataConfig.prior_context_phases describes the earlier context lengths of a resumed run, one ContextPhaseConfig per length. With prior_context_phases set, each source skips the unread rest of the shuffle window it was reading at the switch step and starts its next window, so nothing is served twice. At a 216000-step handoff this skips about 52B tokens, 0.65% of the rest of the run. MixtureDataset takes per-source start offsets to apply the skip. Every phase must give positive weight to the same sources, because a training config drops zero-weight sources and that changes the shuffle keys of the rest; a change in the active sources is rejected. So is a phase at the same sequence length as the one before it, since there a source could continue in place and the skip would only discard data. The seed, the source order, and restoring at the last switch step cannot be checked from the config, so the field docstring states them. The offsets come from each source's true position in the earlier phase, so they also absorb the main-mixture boundary moving from step 108000 to 108096 at 16K. The grug train loop builds its mixture through the new LmDataConfig.train_mixture.

Part of #9615

comments.body:
🤖 Review notes from a walkthrough of the change. None of these block the mechanism; the rename is the main request.

**Rename the prior-phase types.** `PriorDataPhase` is easy to misread: "data" does not say which aspect of the data changed, and in the Harrier code and docs "phase" already means a mixture phase (`_SPEC.phase_weights`, the JSON `phases`, "Phase 1/2/3" in `docs/reports/hero-mixture-log.md`). A context switch can fall in the middle of a mixture phase, so the two divisions of the run need different names. Suggested names:

| Current | Suggested |
| --- | --- |
| `PriorDataPhase` | `ContextPhaseConfig` |
| `LmDataConfig.prior_phases` | `prior_context_phases` |
| `MixturePhase` | `ContextPhase` |

This follows the `FooConfig` → `Foo` pattern: `ContextPhaseConfig` declares a past context phase in steps, and `ContextPhase` is the form `skip_to_window_offsets` uses (start step, `BatchSchedule`, stages in sequence indices). The `ContextPhase` list also holds the current phase. The `MixturePhase` docstring ("A phase of the mixture for ...") should change with it, for example to "One context phase of the run, with its batch schedule and stages in sequence indices." Please also add a sentence to the field docstring that batch-size changes within one context belong in `BatchSchedule`, and that `prior_context_phases` describes earlier context lengths only.

Names and strings that follow from the rename:

- `_prior_phase_offsets` → `_prior_context_phase_offsets`, and `_prior_phase_window_tokens` → `_context_phase_window_tokens`.
- The `"prior_phases ..."` error messages and the `train_mixture` docstring.
- `"Every data phase must draw from the same sources"`, `"Data phases must start at increasing steps"`, and `"Prior phase {phase} must shuffle ..."` → "context phase".
- In `test_context_switch_data.py`: the imports, the `_phase` and `_offsets` annotations, and `test_lm_data_config_prior_phase_resumes_without_repeating_tokens`.
- In #9689: `HarrierPriorContext` and `prior_contexts`, so the stack uses one term. The context history that replaces `CONTEXT_SWITCH_STEP` there (see my comment on #9689) can use the same name.

**Reject adjacent phases with the same sequence length.** `skip_to_window_offsets` accepts two adjacent phases with the same `seq_len`, for example a relaunch that changes only the batch size. In that case the within-window order does not change, so a source could continue at its exact position. `_next_window_start` still rounds up to the next shuffle window and discards up to one window per source (about 537M tokens per source at Harrier's settings). A check that adjacent phases differ in `seq_len` would turn that silent waste into an error. It would also make the `ContextPhase` name exact.

**Rename `counts_before` and make it block-aligned.** `counts_before` does not say what it counts; `sequence_counts_before` does. Its partial-block branch also never runs in this PR: `skip_to_window_offsets` calls it only at block boundaries (rounded up for the old phase, down for the new one). That branch returns a count, but in a partly served block the count is not a read position, because slots are shuffled; a source that served 3 sequences may have served occurrences 0, 7, and 31. Taking a block index instead, as `sequence_counts_before_block(block_id)`, removes the branch and prevents a later caller from using a mid-block count as a position.

**Check source order across phases.** The active-source check compares sets, but order matters as much: it sets each source's shuffle key through `key_iterator`, and the mixture's slot layout through `dataset_index` (including which source receives the rounding remainder). A config that lists the same sources in a different order passes the check and gets a different data layout. Recording the source order in the prior phase and comparing lists would catch this; at minimum, the docstring should say the order must not change.

**Document two assumptions that cannot be checked here.** (1) The shuffle and mixture keys come from the trainer seed, so the seed must be the same in every phase. (2) The offsets assume the current phase starts reading at the last `end_step`. A launch that restores a checkpoint from before that step would re-read data. #9689's trigger checks this for the hero; a docstring sentence on `prior_phases` would cover other callers.

**Optional: give a prior phase a `BatchSchedule`.** `PriorDataPhase.batch_size` is an `int`, so a prior phase cannot have a batch ramp, while the current phase takes a full `BatchSchedule`. A `BatchSchedule` field would give prior and current phases one representation.

**Possible follow-up, not for this PR.** Batch-size history (`BatchSchedule`) and context-length history (`prior_phases`) are both step-indexed descriptions of the run's shape, and could become one schedule. That needs three things this PR should not take on: the trainer must reject a `seq_len` change after the current step, because `Pos` is fixed per launch, while it can follow a batch change; `BatchSchedule` is used in 28 Python files; and the Harrier stage schedule would need to record the realized step of past stage boundaries instead of rounding them again for each batch size.

🤖 Addressed in new commits on top of the reviewed head ([compare 5a2525a4ec..748ad7fe6f](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/compare/5a2525a4ec..748ad7fe6f)):

- **Rename** (86fff8f63b): `ContextPhaseConfig`, `prior_context_phases`, `ContextPhase`, `_prior_context_phase_offsets`, `_context_phase_window_tokens`, the error messages, the `ContextPhase` docstring, and the test names. The field docstring now says that batch-size changes within one context length belong in `BatchSchedule`. In #9689, b596fe391c renames `HarrierPriorContext` and `prior_contexts` to `HarrierContextPhase` and `prior_context_phases`.
- **Same-length adjacent phases** (4ca2f1ba0d): `skip_to_window_offsets` now raises an error.
- **`counts_before`** (c7bdbe68f1): now `sequence_counts_before_block(block_id)`, without the partial-block branch.
- **Source order** (1c99ccec06): documented, not checked. A recorded source list would not catch the case that matters: the Harrier launcher rebuilds the prior phase from the same spec at every launch, so a reordered spec changes the recorded list and the current list together.
- **Seed and restore step** (1c99ccec06): both assumptions are in the `prior_context_phases` docstring.
- **Batch schedule for a prior phase** (748ad7fe6f): `ContextPhaseConfig.batch_size` is now `int | IntSchedule`, the same type as `TrainerConfig.train_batch_size`, so the existing `BatchSchedule(...)` conversion handles both.

The unified schedule is left for a follow-up, as suggested. The `CONTEXT_SWITCH_STEP` history from the #9689 comment is not in these commits.

topics.title: [grug] Select the hero router's top-k experts with a Triton kernel
topics.body:
The hero router's top-(K+1) expert selection runs in a Triton kernel instead of a full XLA sort of every row: 0.096 ms per call instead of 0.856 ms at [65536, 384], k = 9 on one GB200, once in the forward and again in the recompute. The indices and their order match `jax.lax.top_k` bitwise for every input, including ties, signed zeros, infinities and NaNs.

XLA:GPU uses its own top-k kernel only for rows of at least 1,024 elements, so 384-expert rows fall back to a sort. The new kernel takes float32 rows narrower than 1,024 on a GPU device; everything else keeps `jax.lax.top_k`. Its gate asks the default device whether it is a GPU, because a hero test stubs `jax.default_backend` to trace a GPU-only path on CPU devices. The Triton gather-sum's gate makes the same check.

One warp holds one row in registers, as one power-of-two tile or, when that pads less, three equal ones (a 384-wide row is three 128-wide tiles), and takes k successive maxima over XLA's float32 total-order key, breaking ties by the lower column. A row in one warp keeps both reductions inside the warp; Triton reduces across warps through shared memory. A taken or absent entry gets the smallest key and the column n, which the lowest-column reduction never returns, so a negative NaN with payload 0xFFFFFFFF, whose key is also the smallest, is not mistaken for one. The kernel reads an int32 view of the input, so autodiff never asks it for a JVP rule. For k above 16 the steps run in a loop, which compiles in 0.2 s where unrolled steps take 36 s at k = 384.

No rack run measured this kernel alone. On one 64-GPU hero rack (restore step-180000, seed 0, 100 steps), an earlier version that took 0.125 ms per call shortened the step by 0.53%.

Split from #9708. Part of #9636.

evalchemy209.title: Make Evalchemy results and resume state FineStore native
evalchemy209.body:
Write evaluation aggregates, normalized samples, and request checkpoints directly to FineStore. The evaluator restores committed requests by default and skips a completed result before model setup. Results and samples enter the archive in one transaction, so a retry leaves a completed result unchanged.

`--output_path` and `--finestore_output_path` now select the same FineStore archive. Existing scripts keep `--output_path` and use distinct archive paths for distinct evaluations. Remove native JSON/JSONL result serialization, SQLite resume state, and temporary output staging. The serve-and-eval runner and regression gate read the same archive. Concurrent writers to one archive have not been exercised locally.

Part of marin-community/marin#9972. The Marin retry work is tracked in marin-community/marin#9813.
